data.title: STOCKS | Trump Energy Official Says Export Ban Would Not Lower U.S. Fuel Prices
data.description:
U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said a ban on fuel or crude exports would not reduce retail oil prices. According to Sina Finance, Burgum made the remarks on Monday on the sidelines of the G20 energy summit in Houston.

Retail diesel prices have hit a record above $6 per gallon, while gasoline prices have topped $4 per gallon, prompting speculation that the Trump administration could consider export restrictions ahead of key midterm elections. Industry analysts and market observers remain divided on whether such restrictions could ease pressure on consumers over the long term.

Burgum said the administration would consider an export ban only if it believed such a move could lower prices, adding that this was not the case. He and Energy Secretary Chris Wright have publicly opposed such restrictions.

data.title: Federal Judge Orders EPA to Reverse Reclassification of California Clean Air Act Waivers
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, a U.S. federal judge ruled that the Environmental Protection Agency must withdraw its decision to reclassify two Clean Air Act waivers granted to California as "rules" rather than "orders," and must "withdraw or correct" the move in all public statements while preventing the reclassification from taking effect. Congress is moving ahead with votes to use the Congressional Review Act to overturn the waivers, and the House plans to vote on two resolutions introduced in August on Tuesday and Thursday.

data.title: Mauritania Summons Iranian Ambassador Over 'Unacceptable' Actions
data.description: Mauritania's Foreign Ministry summoned Iran's ambassador on September 14 local time and lodged a formal protest over certain actions and activities it said were "inconsistent with diplomatic norms and traditions," according to Jiemian News. The ministry said it wants the Iranian mission to strictly follow diplomatic norms and relevant rules, respect Mauritania's sovereignty, and refrain from interfering in its internal affairs, while still hoping to maintain bilateral ties. Mauritanian officials have not disclosed what specifically triggered the diplomatic dispute, and Iran had not responded as of the report.

data.title: Venezuela's Acting President Delcy Rodriguez Plans to Attend UN General Assembly
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, people familiar with the matter said Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodriguez, plans to travel to New York next week to attend the United Nations General Assembly. The trip would be an important step in the rapid normalization of relations between Caracas and the Trump administration.

People familiar with the matter said Rodriguez would be the first Venezuelan head of state to attend the assembly in nearly a decade. The last was Nicolas Maduro, who attended in September 2018 during U.S. President Donald Trump's first term. Sources said Rodriguez is expected to hold several high-level meetings in New York, and U.S. President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have both said they could meet her if the trip goes ahead.

data.title: China Tightens Exit Rules For Tech Export Violations
data.description: According to CNBC, China is formally restricting its citizens from leaving the country if they violate tech export controls, with the new rules taking effect Tuesday. The measures build on oversight of overseas investment that began July 1 and are aimed at closing loopholes that allowed people and money to leave China without Beijing's approval. Shuai Peng, CEO of Lex Magister, said companies expanding abroad need to assess compliance, especially when executives are negotiating overseas. He said semiconductor and artificial intelligence firms are likely to be most affected, though the rules apply across industries, and he does not expect them to materially limit participation in international conferences such as CES in Las Vegas. Guo Shan, a partner at Hutong Research, said the impact will likely be concentrated in Singapore and Japan, but not on broader global business sentiment toward China.

data.title: Balancer Proposal to Wind Down Treasury and Distribute Assets to BAL Holders Goes to Forum
data.description:
Balancer said a proposal written by Marcus Hardt to wind down Balancer and distribute the treasury to BAL holders has been posted on the forum. According to ChainCatcher, discussion is now open, and Snapshot voting is expected to take place from September 25 to 29.

The project said there is no change for now: pools and withdrawal functions continue to operate as they do currently. Any wind-down action will wait for the voting result.

data.title: Derive Forum User Proposes V3 Migration and Shutdown of Derive Chain
data.description:
Derive forum user domrom submitted a DIP proposal on September 13 to deploy Derive V3, a zkVM program settled on Ethereum mainnet, migrate all V2 positions and balances into the V3 genesis state, move bridged funds to L1, and shut down Derive Chain after the migration is completed. According to ChainCatcher, the proposal said Derive accounted for about 95% of on-chain options premium volume over the previous 30 days as of September 7, 2026, with open interest of about $2 billion.

The proposal describes V3 as a zero-knowledge exchange in which the matching engine and sequencer state transitions are executed in a zkVM and verified on Ethereum L1, while user funds are held in L1 contracts. It said the target is L2Beat Stage 1. The migration would not require new deposits and would use a snapshot of Derive Chain to generate the genesis state. stDRV would be deployed on Ethereum mainnet, and DRV OFT would connect to Robinhood Chain.

If approved, the timeline would require at least 14 days' notice before migration. Bridge transfers would be frozen, trading paused, and a post-settlement snapshot taken before trading resumes. Rewards can be claimed on Optimism until February 1, 2027.

data.title: CrowdStrike CEO Says Slowing AI Model Development Won't Eliminate Security Risks
data.description:
According to CNBC, CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said slowing the development of more powerful artificial intelligence models would not remove the security risks they pose. Speaking on CNBC's "Mad Money," Kurtz said dangerous frontier and open-weight models are already available and argued that cybersecurity protections are needed regardless of whether AI labs slow development. He said AI agents can bypass training or built-in safeguards, creating a need for another layer of security that monitors them at runtime.

CrowdStrike shares rose nearly 14% on Monday to a record-high close above $235, while Palo Alto Networks gained just over 13%. Kurtz also warned against government regulation that he said could hurt U.S. competitiveness in AI and said developers and cybersecurity firms should work together to improve safety in both the lab and production.

data.title: Broadcom CEO Says AI Revenue Targets Stand Despite Model Development Slowdown Fears
data.description: According to CNBC, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said he has not changed his fiscal 2027 and 2028 AI semiconductor forecasts despite investor concern that a slowdown in frontier AI model development could curb chip demand. Tan said Broadcom still sees strong and durable demand for compute infrastructure, AI development, frontier models and inference, and he said Anthropic is on track to become Broadcom's largest custom chip customer in 2027 and remain so in 2028. On Broadcom's fiscal 2026 third-quarter earnings call on Sept. 2, Tan forecast AI semiconductor revenue of $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. Broadcom shares fell 4.8% on Monday, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped 5.6%.

data.title: Iran-Gulf Arab Meeting Delayed as Attacks Near Key Energy Routes Raise Supply Uncertainty
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, a meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states scheduled for the day was delayed, while a series of attacks near key Middle East energy transport routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, further increased uncertainty over global energy supplies. Oman News Agency said on the 13th that Oman stated the meeting, originally set to be held in the southern city of Salalah, would be postponed to create conditions for constructive dialogue, and Omani Foreign Minister Badr said on social media that Oman would continue to promote dialogue and foster regional stability and lasting cooperation.

data.title: Polymarket Dodgers-Reds Submarket Sees Sharp Odds Swing
data.description: A Polymarket submarket tied to the Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Cincinnati Reds game saw the Cincinnati Reds option in the first five innings run line -1.5 jump from 17.5% one hour earlier to 49.5%, according to Catcher Predict monitoring. According to ChainCatcher, the move reflected a 32% swing and was flagged as potentially affected by breaking news.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Google Allows All Engineers to Use Anthropic's Claude
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Google allows all engineers to use Anthropic PBC's Claude model.

data.title: Oracle: U.S. court pause order applies only to microgrid permit, not data center
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Oracle said a U.S. court pause order applies only to the microgrid permit, not the data center, and that it will continue working on the data center issue in New Mexico.

data.title: U.S. President Donald Trump?
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, California Governor Gavin Newsom said he would not run if former Vice President Kamala Harris enters the 2028 presidential race, ruling out a possible Democratic primary matchup between the two best-known Democrats from California. "I don't know whether she will run; we'll see," Newsom said in a video interview released on Monday.

data.title: Authentic Brands Group Eyes IPO as Early as First Half of Next Year
data.description: Authentic Brands Group, which licenses Elvis Presley’s image and the Reebok sportswear brand, could pursue an initial public stock offering as early as the first half of next year, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Kraft Bars Macklemore From Boston Stop on Ed Sheeran Tour
data.description:
Robert Kraft barred Macklemore from appearing during the Boston leg of Ed Sheeran’s concert tour after the rapper made pro-Palestinian comments at a recent show, according to Bloomberg.

The source said Kraft’s protest led to Macklemore being dropped from the appearance.

data.title: Senate Democrats Remain Split Over Clarity Act Ethics Provisions
data.description: More Senate Democrats who had been willing to support the Clarity Act remain dissatisfied with the bill’s current ethics provisions, according to reports by Eleanor Mueller and Brendan Pedersen. According to Odaily, Ruben Gallego and Angela Alsobrooks, who backed Senate Banking Committee Republicans’ effort to advance the bill out of committee in May, have not yet taken a position, while Kirsten Gillibrand is urging colleagues to vote yes tomorrow so the measure can move to full Senate consideration and further debate.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent Says CLARITY Act Is Key to U.S. Tech Competition
data.description:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the CLARITY Act is critical to helping the United States win the global competition in new technologies. According to ChainCatcher, he said the GENIUS Act was passed to ensure that stablecoin infrastructure, which he described as a revolutionary financial technology, is built in the United States.

Bessent said protecting the continued health of the U.S. community banking sector has been a consistent focus since he took office. He said the administration’s dual emphasis on promoting new digital technologies and adjusting community bank regulation is key to economic growth, and that the final draft of the CLARITY Act advances that mission by giving the Treasury secretary additional authority to act if deposit outflows change and harm community banks.

He added that if stablecoins damage community banks, he would not hesitate to use those tools to ensure they are fully protected. Bessent said community banks are vital to U.S. economic performance and Main Street growth, and that economic security is national security.

data.title: SBF Lawyer Says $11 Billion Fine Would Leave Him Poor Forever
data.description: Sam Bankman-Fried’s Supreme Court lawyer says the $11 billion penalty tied to his sentence would leave the FTX founder broke for life after prison. According to BeInCrypto, Jeffrey Fisher argued the money judgment violates the Eighth Amendment ban on excessive fines and said no realistic future earnings could ever repay it. Fisher also said jurors heard customers lost billions but were not told they would be repaid, which he says denied SBF a fair trial.

data.title: Japan Ministries Propose Just 17 Billion Yen in Budget Cuts
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, Japanese government ministries and agencies have proposed budget cuts totaling just 17 billion yen ($110 million) so far under Tokyo's version of the U.S. DOGE budget efficiency initiative. The figure suggests limited appetite in the bureaucracy for spending reductions.
